Recursive Reasoning Dataset API

This page documents the trainer-facing dataset utilities in gollek-ml-recursive-reasoning.

Use this API when a structured reasoning benchmark needs to produce examples, split them into train/validation/test partitions, profile the data, and hand backend-neutral padded mini-batches to a trainer.

See also:

  • Recursive Reasoning Docs
  • Recursive Reasoning Dataset Workflow
  • gollek-ml-recursive-reasoning API Reference

Data Flow

benchmark adapter
  -> DiscreteTokenDatasetExample
  -> DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanner
  -> DiscreteTokenDatasetProfiler
  -> DiscreteTokenDatasetSplitter
  -> DiscreteTokenDatasetEpochBatcher
  -> DiscreteTokenDatasetBatch
  -> trainer/model backend

The data flow is intentionally independent of ONNX, SafeTensor, GGUF, LiteRT, Metal, CUDA, or any tensor implementation. Tensor conversion happens after the batch is built.

One-Call Dataset Plan

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanner composes the common trainer-data flow from one config:

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanConfig config =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanConfig.stratifiedLengthSorted(
        0.10,   // validation fraction
        0.10,   // test fraction
        2026L,  // split seed
        32,     // train batch size
        64,     // validation/test batch size
        -1      // input and target pad token
    );

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlan plan =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanner.plan(examples, config);

The plan includes:

Field API
Full profile plan.profile()
Train/validation/test split plan.split()
Training epoch plan.trainEpoch()
Validation epoch plan.validationEpoch()
Test epoch plan.testEpoch()
Training padding rate plan.trainPaddingRate()
Pre-training diagnostics plan.diagnostics()
Policy-driven diagnostics plan.diagnostics(policy)
Readiness report plan.readiness(gate)
Plan fingerprint plan.fingerprint()
Preflight report plan.report(gate)

Use the planner for the standard path. Use the lower-level profiler, splitter, and epoch batcher directly when a research experiment needs custom control.

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnostics reports:

Metric API
Split sizes trainCount(), validationCount(), testCount()
Batch counts trainBatchCount(), validationBatchCount(), testBatchCount()
Training examples emittedTrainingExamples(), droppedTrainingExamples()
Known-solution coverage knownSolutionCoverageRate()
Training padding trainPaddingRate(), trainPaddingTokenCount()
Per-task split coverage taskSplits()
Warnings warnings(), hasWarnings()
Readiness isReadyForTraining()
Compact status status() returning ready, warning, or blocked
Report export toMetadata()

Warnings cover empty datasets, empty train/validation/test splits, dropped training examples, missing or partial known-solution coverage, and high training padding rate. For mixed-task datasets, diagnostics also warn when a task is missing from train, validation, or test while that global split exists.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnosticsPolicy when warning expectations differ by environment. defaults() preserves the normal pre-training checks, lenient() keeps only hard blockers such as empty datasets or empty train splits, and custom policies can tune the high-padding threshold or disable specific optional warnings.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessGate to convert diagnostics into a trainer decision. training() accepts warning-bearing plans that are still trainable, strict() blocks warnings for CI or production runs, and lenient() uses the lenient diagnostics policy before evaluating readiness.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprint to stamp checkpoints or CI reports with a stable SHA-256 digest. fromExamples(...) hashes ordered examples, while plan.fingerprint() hashes the planning config, split partitions, example tokens/metadata, and epoch batch layout. fromMetadata(...) recreates a stored fingerprint from direct checkpoint metadata, and fromMetadataSection(...) extracts it from a larger report/checkpoint map.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprintMatch before resuming from a checkpoint. plan.verifyFingerprint(expected), plan.verifyFingerprintMetadata(metadata), plan.verifyFingerprintMetadataSection(reportMetadata), report.verifyFingerprint(expected), report.verifyFingerprintMetadata(metadata), and report.verifyFingerprintMetadataSection(reportMetadata) return a match report with mismatch reasons and requireMatch() for fail-fast resume guards.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReport when a trainer wants the whole preflight bundle in one place: fingerprint, diagnostics, readiness decision, summary, and metadata export. DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReport.fromMetadata(...) rehydrates that payload from JSON metadata so CI tools and checkpoint inspectors can re-run resume preflight checks without rematerializing the full dataset.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointManifest when checkpoint metadata should also carry experiment/run identity, model family, seed, checkpoint step, creator, timestamp, and custom attributes alongside the dataset preflight report. Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineage when that manifest should also carry experiment ancestry. New manifests default to a root lineage, while lineageFrom(parentSnapshot) records the parent run id, parent step, parent dataset fingerprint, relation, generation, and optional lineage attributes. Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageGraph when a checkpoint root should resolve that ancestry across multiple sidecars, expose the selected root-to-leaf lineage chain, and flag duplicate run ids, missing parents, or ambiguous parent references. It also verifies that the recorded parent step and dataset fingerprint match the resolved parent checkpoint. Its health metadata reports parent identity mismatches and lineage cycles, and exposes a compact CI-oriented issue summary with issueDetails entries for affected checkpoint paths, stable issue codes, severity, blocking status, issue-specific reasons, and remediation actions. The health metadata also includes issueCodes, issueDetailCount, blockingIssueCount, primaryIssueCode, and primaryIssueAction for compact automation gates, plus top-level kind and schemaVersion fields that identify the stable health payload contract. Use healthSnapshot() or DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageHealthSnapshot.fromMetadata(...) when extensions, CI jobs, or dashboards need a typed read-side contract instead of raw map parsing. Use jsonSchemaMetadata() when those consumers need the bundled checkpoint-lineage-health.v1.schema.json contract for validation or schema registry publishing. Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageHealthValidationReport or validateMetadata(...), validateJson(...), and validatePath(...) when a CI job or extension needs a compact valid/invalid report with stable codes instead of throwing on malformed payloads. Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageHealthValidationReport.jsonSchemaMetadata() when consumers also need the stable validation-report schema, or DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageHealthSchemaCatalog.catalogMetadata(true) when they need to discover both health contracts together with embedded schemas. Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageHealthSchemaCatalog.jsonSchemaMetadata() when consumers need to pin the schema-catalog contract itself. The catalog includes a bundle-level schemaSetSha256, per-schema SHA-256 digests, and byte counts for drift checks. Use catalogSnapshot(...) when Java consumers need typed accessors such as schemaSetSha256(), schemaSetIdentity(), matchesSchemaSet(...), requireSchemaSet(...), contractNames(), contractDetails(), contractsByName(), contractDetail(...), requireContractDetail(...), contractsByPayloadKind(), contractsByJsonSchemaId(), contractForJsonSchemaId(...), requireContractForJsonSchemaId(...), contractForPayloadSchema(...), requireContractForPayloadSchema(...), hasEmbeddedSchemas(), and requireCurrentSchema(...) for compact or embedded-schema catalog payloads. The typed contract entries expose name(), payloadKind(), payloadSchemaVersion(), jsonSchemaId(), jsonSchemaSha256(), jsonSchemaByteCount(), optional catalog-only metadata such as jsonSchemaResource() and inspectorSections(), plus schemaMetadata() when schemas are embedded. DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaContract is the reusable descriptor behind each schema resource, digest, byte count, and embedded schema metadata entry. DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaBundle composes those contracts into a catalog, compact lock payload, and valid/invalid lock-validation report so future trainer artifacts can publish the same drift-check surface without copying lineage-health-specific catalog logic. Prefer DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaBundle.builder(...) for new bundles; it keeps the catalog, lock, validator, label, code, and contract sections explicit and rejects duplicate contract names before they can produce ambiguous lock comparisons. Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageHealthSchemaCatalog.lockMetadata() when CI needs a compact lock payload without embedded schemas, or lockSnapshot() when Java consumers need typed accessors such as schemaSetSha256(), schemaSetIdentity(), matchesSchemaSet(...), requireSchemaSet(...), schemaCount(), contractNames(), contractDetails(), contractsByName(), contractDetail(...), requireContractDetail(...), contractsByPayloadKind(), contractsByJsonSchemaId(), contractForJsonSchemaId(...), requireContractForJsonSchemaId(...), contractForPayloadSchema(...), requireContractForPayloadSchema(...), and requireCurrentSchema(...) for that same payload. Use lockJsonSchemaMetadata() to validate that lock payload. Use validateLockMetadata(...) or validateCurrentLock() when CI needs a stable valid/invalid report comparing a saved lock with the current schema bundle, and validateLockJson(...) or validateLockPath(...) when that saved lock is still JSON text or a file. Use validateLockSnapshot(...) when the saved lock has already been rehydrated as a DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaLockSnapshot. Use requireValidLockMetadata(...), requireValidLockJson(...), requireValidLockPath(...), or requireCurrentLockValid() when the same check should fail fast on drift. Use the ...Report(...) variants when Java consumers want a DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaLockValidationReport with typed accessors such as valid(), mismatchCount(), expectedSchemaSetIdentity(), actualSchemaSetIdentity(), schemaSetIdentityMatch(), requireSchemaSetIdentityMatch(), mismatchPaths(), mismatchDetails(), firstMismatch(), hasMismatchAtPath(...), mismatchesForType(...), mismatchesByPath(), and requireValid(). mismatchDetails() returns typed DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaLockMismatch entries with type(), path(), expected(), actual(), and summary() while preserving the raw JSON-shaped map through toMetadata(). Use lockValidationJsonSchemaMetadata() when the validation report shape must be pinned by external tooling. The report includes its validation schema id/resource and the expected/actual lock-schema ids so persisted CI logs can be interpreted without extra context. Use healthScore, alertLevel, and healthBadge for UI status rendering. Use checks, failingChecks, and checkSummary for category-level lineage invariant rows, primary failing-check identity, type, action, full check payload, and severity rollups; those priority-aware primary failing-check fields are also mirrored at the top level of healthMetadata().

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointManifestSnapshot on resume paths to rehydrate persisted manifest metadata, verify schema/fingerprint/readiness consistency, and compare the checkpoint dataset fingerprint with a freshly materialized plan.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReport when the trainer wants one checkpoint-resume preflight object that combines schema compatibility, stored dataset readiness, and fingerprint matching before opening checkpoint state. When constructed from a current DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReport, it also blocks resume if the freshly materialized report is not accepted by the current gate. Call gateSummary(), gates(), gateAccepted(...), requireGateAccepted(...), requireAllGatesAccepted(), blockedGates(), or warningGates() when extensions need a stable automation view of each resume guard: manifest schema, checkpoint dataset readiness, dataset fingerprint, resume expectation, and current dataset plan readiness. The summary exposes counts, blocked/warning ids, grouped gate ids and counts by status, severity, per-category rollups, category status lists, primary blocked or warning gate ids/categories, primary headline gate fields, highest severity, and compact attention/action flags plus a render-ready badge for dashboards or CI logs. Each gate also carries a stable actionCode() and human actionHint(); the summary and badge expose the primary action so automation can branch on the code while UI surfaces can show the hint directly. Use nextActions() when a report has multiple blockers or warnings: it returns blocked actions first, warning actions second, and a single continue action only for a fully ready resume decision. actionCodes(), requiredActionCodes(), and warningActionCodes() are compact shortcuts for CI rules. Prefer actionPlan() when an extension or dashboard wants the full handoff in one object, including ready flags, counts, primary action, ordered actions, and compact metadata. Resume reports and read-side snapshots expose actionPlan(), readinessBadge(), and the action shortcut lists directly, and toMetadata() includes top-level actionPlan and readinessBadge aliases for tools that do not want to traverse gateSummary. DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeActionPlan.fromMetadata(...), DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeAction.fromMetadata(...), and DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReadinessBadge.fromMetadata(...) rehydrate those handoff payloads for extensions that receive only JSON. DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeGateCategorySummary.fromMetadata(...) validates a single category rollup against the detailed resume gates when a dashboard wants category-level rows without trusting stale derived counts. Call explanation() on the resume report when a trainer, extension, or CI job needs stable finding codes such as dataset-fingerprint-mismatch, checkpoint-schema-mismatch, or current-plan-rejected plus suggested next steps. DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeExplanation.fromMetadata(...) rehydrates that payload from JSON and verifies its derived primary code, primary category, and finding count.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeExpectation when that preflight should also require a specific experiment name, run id, model family, seed, exact checkpoint step, or minimum checkpoint step.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumePolicy when trainer resume code wants one reusable object that chooses the current readiness gate, applies optional resume compatibility, and enforces optional identity expectations. Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeCompatibilityMode.STRICT for exact resume safety, COMPATIBLE for warning-only current-plan compatibility, and FORCE only when a research/debug workflow intentionally continues through dataset fingerprint or current-plan mismatches with warnings. DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumePolicy.fromMetadata(...) rehydrates that policy from persisted trainer config or CI metadata. Reports produced through a policy include policyTracked() and policyMetadata() so trainer audit payloads can show the exact gate and expectation settings used for the decision.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReportSnapshot when dashboards, CI, or extensions need to read a persisted resume-report sidecar without materializing the dataset plan again. It preserves the resume status, rejection reasons, gate summary, gate list, policy metadata, checkpoint identity, and current-plan report payload. Snapshot loading validates a persisted gateSummary, top-level actionPlan, and top-level readinessBadge against the detailed gates when present, validates derived grouped gate indexes when present, and synthesizes gates, summary, and grouped indexes for older sidecars that predate those fields.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSnapshot when those tools need the whole checkpoint-directory sidecar state in one read. It loads the manifest, detects whether a resume report exists, reports manifest-only versus ready or blocked states, and exposes a compact trainingReportMetadata() payload.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointInventory when tools need to scan a root directory of checkpoint runs. It reports ready, blocked, manifest-only, and failed sidecar reads, and can select the latest ready checkpoint by manifest creation time.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSelectionPolicy when those tools need the same restore choice everywhere. latestReady() allows manifest-only checkpoints, latestResumeReady() requires a persisted ready resume report, and the strict variants fail if the inventory contains corrupt sidecars. Add withFailOnLineageIssues(true) when a resume path should also reject checkpoint roots with duplicate run ids, missing parents, ambiguous parents, parent identity mismatches, or cycles before selecting a checkpoint.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointInspectionReport when tools need to show why a checkpoint was or was not selected. It keeps accepted and rejected candidate decisions, selected checkpoint metadata, strict inventory failure details, and a JSON-friendly toMetadata() payload together.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePlan when trainer resume code needs the selected checkpoint as a typed handoff. It keeps the root directory, checkpoint directory, manifest path, resume-report path, policy, checkpoint identity, resume readiness, and JSON-friendly toMetadata() payload together. Create one with inspection.requireRestorePlan(), inventory.requireRestorePlan(policy), or DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointBridge.requireRestorePlan(root, policy).

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePreflight as the final guard before opening checkpoint state. It combines the selected restore plan with a fresh current-plan DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReport, so a checkpoint can be selected by identity and persisted readiness but still be blocked if the current dataset plan fingerprint, gate, or expectation no longer matches. It also exposes gateSummary(), nextActions(), actionPlan(), readinessBadge(), requireAllGatesAccepted(), requireNoRequiredActions(), and requireMetadataMatch(...) directly, and its metadata includes top-level actionPlan and readinessBadge aliases for CLI and CI consumers.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointMetadataJson when checkpoint metadata needs dependency-free JSON persistence. It provides deterministic toJson(...) / toPrettyJson(...), immutable fromJson(...), file write(...) / read(...), readSnapshot(...), readPlanReport(...), and readResumeReportSnapshot(...) helpers for checkpoint manifest, dataset plan report, and resume-report files.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerProvenanceSpec as the normal trainer-facing entry point. It builds the plan report, manifest, resume policy, sidecar paths, bridge helpers, restore-selection policy, restore-plan helpers, and lifecycle listener from one immutable setup object, which keeps extensions from hand-wiring the same checkpoint provenance flow.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointBridge when that metadata should live beside canonical trainer checkpoints. It writes stable discrete-token-dataset-manifest.json and discrete-token-dataset-resume-report.json sidecars, runs resume preflight from the checkpoint directory, applies checkpoint selection policies across a root of runs, returns typed restore plans for selected checkpoints, and can attach a recursiveReasoningDataset section to trainer summary metadata.

Use DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerProvenanceListener when the trainer should perform that sidecar workflow from lifecycle callbacks. It writes the manifest at training start, validates an existing manifest before overwriting it when a current plan is supplied, and keeps the enriched TrainingSummary available through lastEnrichedSummary().

toMetadata() returns an immutable Map<String, Object> with nested split, batches, trainingExamples, trainPadding, and taskSplits sections. Use it when writing checkpoint metadata, JBang inspector payloads, or CI summaries.

Each DiscreteTokenDatasetTaskSplitDiagnostics entry reports:

Field Meaning
taskId() Benchmark/task label
exampleCount() Total examples for that task
trainCount() Examples in train
validationCount() Examples in validation
testCount() Examples in test
trainRate() Train share for that task
validationRate() Validation share for that task
testRate() Test share for that task

Token Example

DiscreteTokenDatasetExample is the canonical single-example record for structured reasoning datasets.

Required fields:

Field Type Meaning
taskId String Stable benchmark label such as nqueens, graph-coloring, or arc-grid
exampleIndex int Non-negative source index
inputTokens int[] Non-empty input token sequence
targetTokens int[] Non-empty target token sequence
knownSolutionCount int -1 when unknown, otherwise >= 1
metadata Map<String, Object> Optional immutable per-example metadata

Example:

DiscreteTokenDatasetExample example = new DiscreteTokenDatasetExample(
    "graph-coloring",
    0,
    new int[] {0, -1, -1, 1},
    new int[] {0, 2, 1, 1},
    3,
    Map.of("nodeCount", 4, "colorCount", 3)
);

Benchmark-specific examples can adapt into this shape:

DiscreteTokenDatasetExample nQueens = nQueensExample.toTokenExample();
DiscreteTokenDatasetExample coloring = graphColoringExample.toTokenExample();

Dataset Profile

DiscreteTokenDatasetProfiler.profile(examples) returns a DiscreteTokenDatasetProfile.

It reports:

Metric API
Example count exampleCount()
Task mix taskExampleCounts()
Input length stats inputLengths()
Target length stats targetLengths()
Observed token count observedTokenCount()
Distinct token count distinctTokenCount()
Token range minToken(), maxToken()
Known-solution coverage knownSolutionExampleCount(), knownSolutionCoverageRate()

Example:

DiscreteTokenDatasetProfile profile =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetProfiler.profile(examples);

System.out.println(profile.taskExampleCounts());
System.out.println(profile.inputLengths().maxLength());
System.out.println(profile.knownSolutionCoverageRate());

DiscreteTokenLengthStats stores compact min/max/total/mean length stats for input or target sequences.

Train/Validation/Test Split

DiscreteTokenDatasetSplitter provides deterministic split policies.

Exact-count splits:

DiscreteTokenDatasetSplit split =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetSplitter.sequentialByCounts(
        examples,
        100,  // validation examples
        100   // test examples
    );

Fraction splits:

DiscreteTokenDatasetSplit split =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetSplitter.shuffledByFractions(
        examples,
        0.10,
        0.10,
        42L
    );

Task-stratified fraction splits:

DiscreteTokenDatasetSplit split =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetSplitter.stratifiedShuffledByFractions(
        examples,
        0.10,
        0.10,
        42L
    );

Use stratified splits when one dataset mixes several benchmark families. The splitter groups examples by taskId, applies the same floor-fraction policy inside each task group, then concatenates train, validation, and test partitions.

Convenience profile methods:

DiscreteTokenDatasetProfile allProfile = split.profile();
DiscreteTokenDatasetProfile trainProfile = split.trainProfile();
DiscreteTokenDatasetProfile validProfile = split.validationProfile();
DiscreteTokenDatasetProfile testProfile = split.testProfile();

Epoch Builder

DiscreteTokenDatasetEpochBatcher materializes padded mini-batches for one epoch.

Sequential:

DiscreteTokenDatasetEpoch epoch =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetEpochBatcher.sequential(
        split.trainExamples(),
        32,
        -1,
        -1,
        false
    );

Seeded shuffle:

DiscreteTokenDatasetEpoch epoch =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetEpochBatcher.shuffled(
        split.trainExamples(),
        32,
        -1,
        2026L,
        false
    );

Length sorted:

DiscreteTokenDatasetEpoch epoch =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetEpochBatcher.lengthSorted(
        split.trainExamples(),
        32,
        -1,
        false
    );

Length sorting groups shorter examples together before batching. It is useful when input or target lengths vary, because it reduces padding capacity without coupling the dataset layer to a tensor backend.

DiscreteTokenDatasetEpoch reports:

Metric API
Number of mini-batches batchCount()
Emitted examples emittedExampleCount()
Dropped examples droppedExampleCount()
Observed tokens observedTokenCount()
Padded capacity paddedTokenCapacity()
Padding tokens paddingTokenCount()
Padding rate paddingRate()

Padded Batch

DiscreteTokenDatasetBatcher.batch(...) pads a list of examples into one DiscreteTokenDatasetBatch.

DiscreteTokenDatasetBatch batch =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetBatcher.batch(examples, -1, -1);

The batch includes:

Field Shape Meaning
inputTokens() [batch, maxInputLength] Padded input tokens
targetTokens() [batch, maxTargetLength] Padded target tokens
inputMask() [batch, maxInputLength] 1 for real tokens, 0 for padding
targetMask() [batch, maxTargetLength] 1 for real tokens, 0 for padding
inputLengths() [batch] Original input lengths
targetLengths() [batch] Original target lengths
knownSolutionCounts() [batch] -1 or known solution count
metadata() list Per-example metadata

All public array accessors return defensive copies.

Practical Defaults

Recommended starter policy:

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanConfig config =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanConfig.stratifiedLengthSorted(
        0.10,
        0.10,
        2026L,
        32,
        64,
        -1
    );

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlan plan =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanner.plan(examples, config);

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnostics diagnostics = plan.diagnostics();
if (diagnostics.hasWarnings()) {
    System.out.println(diagnostics.warnings());
}

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnostics ciDiagnostics = plan.diagnostics(
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnosticsPolicy.defaults()
        .withHighPaddingRateThreshold(0.25)
);

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessReport readiness = plan.readiness(
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessGate.strict()
);
readiness.requireAccepted();

DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprint fingerprint = plan.fingerprint();
Map<String, Object> checkpointFingerprintMetadata = fingerprint.toMetadata();
DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprint expectedFingerprint =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprint.fromMetadata(checkpointFingerprintMetadata);
DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprintMatch resumeMatch =
    plan.verifyFingerprint(expectedFingerprint);
resumeMatch.requireMatch();

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReport report = plan.report(
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessGate.strict()
);
Map<String, Object> reportMetadata = report.toMetadata();
report.verifyFingerprintMetadataSection(reportMetadata).requireMatch();

Path checkpointDir = Path.of("checkpoints/run-001");
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerProvenanceSpec provenance =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerProvenanceSpec.builder(checkpointDir, plan)
        .strict()
        .experimentName("gram-structured-reasoning")
        .runId("run-001")
        .seed(2026L)
        .checkpointStep(12L)
        .exactResumeExpectation()
        .build();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointManifest manifest = provenance.manifest();
Map<String, Object> checkpointMetadata = manifest.toMetadata();
provenance.writeManifest();
Map<String, Object> loadedCheckpointMetadata = provenance.readManifestMetadata();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointManifestSnapshot snapshot =
    provenance.readSnapshot();
snapshot.requireCurrentSchema();
snapshot.verifyPlan(plan).requireMatch();
snapshot.requireDatasetAccepted();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReport resumeReport =
    snapshot.resumeReport(plan);
resumeReport.requireReady();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeExpectation expectedCheckpoint =
    provenance.resumeExpectation();
snapshot.resumeReport(plan, expectedCheckpoint).requireReady();
DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReport currentStrictReport =
    plan.report(DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessGate.strict());
snapshot.resumeReport(currentStrictReport, expectedCheckpoint).requireReady();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumePolicy resumePolicy =
    provenance.resumePolicy();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReport policyReport =
    provenance.requireResumeReadyAndWriteReport();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReportSnapshot persistedResumeAudit =
    provenance.readResumeReportSnapshot();
persistedResumeAudit.requireReady();
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSnapshot checkpointAudit =
    provenance.readCheckpointSnapshot();
checkpointAudit.requireReady();
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointInventory checkpointInventory =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointInventory.scan(checkpointDir.getParent());
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSnapshot latestReadyCheckpoint =
    checkpointInventory.requireLatestReadyCheckpoint();
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSelectionPolicy checkpointSelection =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSelectionPolicy.latestResumeReady()
        .withExpectation(provenance.resumeExpectation());
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSnapshot latestResumeReadyCheckpoint =
    checkpointSelection.require(checkpointInventory);
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSnapshot bridgeSelectedCheckpoint =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointBridge.requireCheckpoint(
        checkpointDir.getParent(),
        checkpointSelection);
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointInspectionReport checkpointInspection =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointBridge.inspectCheckpoints(
        checkpointDir.getParent(),
        checkpointSelection);
checkpointInspection.requireSelectedCheckpoint();
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePlan restorePlan =
    checkpointInspection.requireRestorePlan();
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePreflight restorePreflight =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointBridge.requireRestorePreflightReady(
        restorePlan,
        plan,
        provenance.resumePolicy());
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePlan provenanceRestorePlan =
    provenance.requireRestorePlan();
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePreflight provenanceRestorePreflight =
    provenance.requireRestorePreflightReady();
Map<String, Object> resumeAuditMetadata = policyReport.toMetadata();
Map<String, Object> trainerMetadata =
    provenance.attachToTrainingMetadata(Map.of("runId", "run-001"), policyReport);
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerProvenanceListener provenanceListener =
    provenance.listener();
// Pass provenanceListener to a canonical trainer via .listener(provenanceListener).
TrainingSummary enrichedSummary =
    provenanceListener.lastEnrichedSummary().orElse(null);
Map<String, Object> resumePolicyMetadata = resumePolicy.toMetadata();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumePolicy reloadedResumePolicy =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumePolicy.fromMetadata(resumePolicyMetadata);
reloadedResumePolicy.requireReady(loadedCheckpointMetadata, plan);
String resumeAuditJson =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointMetadataJson.toPrettyJson(resumeAuditMetadata);

Use this when:

  • the dataset mixes multiple structured reasoning tasks
  • sequence lengths vary
  • training wants deterministic repeatability
  • the backend tensor conversion layer should stay separate from data planning

Invariants

The dataset API validates aggressively:

  • examples must have non-empty input and target token sequences
  • knownSolutionCount must be -1 or >= 1
  • batches are rectangular after padding
  • masks must exactly match sequence lengths
  • split fractions must be finite and in [0.0, 1.0]
  • validation plus test fraction must not exceed 1.0
  • batch size must be greater than zero

These checks are meant to fail early before a trainer or backend sees malformed data.
